candidates.title: Stored revert mode: a host I/O error inside a commit makes the CLI's own error-path revert delete the synced <dir> (and, on a failed rename, every copy of the committed state)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: the cartesi-machine CLI). It stands in for an operator implementation that retains its machine across inputs (the manual presents stored mode as the way to run an epoch without a server and keep a durable accepted state).
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua: revert_stored.__index:commit (3893-3918), revert_stored.__index:revert (3920-3929), revert_stored:__close (3941-3943); called from run_advance_state_input (4707 snapshot, 4725 commit) and run_inspect_state_query (4666). Interacts with machine::remove_stored / machine::rename_stored (src/machine.cpp 599-659).
candidates.description: commit() first destroys the machine, syncs <dir> (now an O2-guaranteed directory holding the newly accepted state), clones it to <dir>.revert.tmp and syncs it, then REMOVES the old <dir>.revert (setting self.backup_directory = nil once that succeeds) and renames .tmp to .revert. If anything after the removal starts throws (a failed unlink inside remove_stored, remove_stored's final parent fsync, the rename, the parent fsync inside rename_stored), the error propagates with snapshot_taken still true, so the to-be-closed `backup` runs __close(err) -> revert(). revert() unconditionally does m:destroy(); m:remove_stored(<dir>) and only then tries m:clone_stored(self.backup_directory, <dir>). By then the backup is gone or half removed (or self.backup_directory is nil), so the clone fails, after the synced <dir> has already been deleted. In the rename-failure branch, commit() itself has also removed <dir>.revert.tmp (line 3911) before rethrowing, so all three directories are gone. The original I/O error is then masked by a Lua 'bad argument #1 to clone_stored (string expected, got nil)'. The manual promises the opposite: '<dir>.revert always holds a synced copy of the last committed state', and its recovery rules assume <dir> holds the committed state when only .tmp is present. In the unlink-failure case the leftover names are a partial <dir>.revert, a good <dir>.revert.tmp and no <dir>. The documented rule ('If machine.revert exists, it holds that state, so discard machine and machine.revert.tmp') then discards the only intact copy. In the parent-fsync case (see R6-DYNPERSIST-1), .revert is gone and .tmp is present, so the rule says '<dir> holds that state, .tmp can be discarded', but the CLI has just deleted <dir>.
candidates.trigger: A host I/O fault (EIO, ENOSPC/EDQUOT on rename, failing directory fsync) during the commit that follows an accepted input (or the commit before an inspect query) of `cartesi-machine --revert-mode=stored --load=<dir>,sharing:all --cmio-advance-state=...`, after the old backup removal has started. No adversary is needed beyond the host fault; any guest that accepts an input reaches the commit.
candidates.reachability: Reached on every accepted input in stored mode. The fault is a host fault, which THREAT_MODEL section 4 allows to stop the operator but forbids the emulator to turn into damage of O2-guaranteed directories. No crash or kill is involved: the process keeps running and its own cleanup code deletes the directories.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state' is excluded only with that proviso. Here the host fault is turned into deletion of O2-guaranteed directories (<dir> was 'synced after the last change to its contents' after the machine 'was destroyed without a crash before that sync'), so it is not excluded. It does not need a reload of an unguaranteed directory (O2 exclusion) and is not 'cleaning up after a stop': the process is running. 2. Role: the cartesi-machine CLI is Support (AUDIT.md). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3. High/Medium cases: the Medium case 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash or damage to a directory that O2 guarantees' does not fit, because the guaranteed <dir> (and in the rename case also <dir>.revert.tmp) is destroyed. 4. In the operator role it violates O2 as bound to the tools ('O1 and O2 bind the emulator too. The tools and reference implementations that ship with it must follow them ... A defect ... that damages a directory while O2 guarantees it, is not excused by them') and R4 ('After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim'). That rating is Critical. Capped as Support: Medium. 5. Not Low. Alternative reading: if the CLI's stored mode is only a development tool and nothing computing claims stands behind it, the rating is Low (tool defect).
candidates.threat_to_goal: An operator that retains its machine the documented way loses every durable copy of its committed state on one transient I/O error, or is told by the documented recovery rule to discard the only intact copy. It can then defend its claim only by recomputing from an older retained state (possibly the genesis template), which is the restart cost R12 bounds by 'the nearest retained input boundary'. Every claim and proof computed afterwards depends on a state that the emulator's own error handling destroyed.
candidates.evidence: Scratch dir MANCLIROLL. (a) failrename.c, an LD_PRELOAD shim, fails the 3rd renameat2() (the commit after input 0) with EIO. Ran `cartesi-machine --load=fi/m,clone:<baremetal-template>,sharing:all --revert-mode=stored --cmio-advance-state=input_file_index_begin:0,input_file_index_end:2,output_proof:`. Result: exit 1 with 'bad argument #1 to clone_stored (string expected, got nil)' from revert() via __close. Afterwards fi/m, fi/m.revert and fi/m.revert.tmp do not exist. (b) failunlink.c fails the 30th unlink() under *.revert/, i.e. inside the commit after input 0, with EIO. Result: the error comes from line 3926 (clone from the half-removed backup), and fi/m is gone. m.revert is half removed and does not load ('unable to open backing file ... 0000000000000000-8000.bin'). m.revert.tmp loads and holds the accepted state (mcycle 8506023, 0x8500ec6c...). The documented rule then discards m.revert.tmp.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: build the shim, run the stored-mode epoch on the baremetal-template with 2 accepted inputs and FAIL_RENAME_AT=3 (and a second case with the unlink shim). Then apply the manual's recovery rule to the names left on disk: .revert if present, else <dir> if .tmp is present, else start over. Assert that the directory the rule selects loads, and that its root hash equals the state after input 0, or the committed state before it. The test fails today because nothing loadable remains, or the rule selects a half-removed .revert. Expected fix: do not revert by deleting <dir> once commit has started removing the backup, and do not remove .tmp after a failed rename.

candidates.title: Documented uarch computation-hash shortcut (begin_epoch:false + next_input_offset, 'needs no epoch files') aborts with 'outputs Merkle root mismatch', with no claim, whenever the application has accepted any earlier output
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI, --uarch-cycle-computation-hash with --cmio-advance-state=begin_epoch:false,next_input_offset (src/cartesi-machine.lua initialize_cmio_outputs, flush_pending_outputs, uarch builder) vs doc/README.md 'Computation hashes'
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: the cartesi-machine CLI); here it is a tool that computes uarch-level claims.
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua: initialize_cmio_outputs (3533-3557) starts an empty host outputs frontier when begin_epoch:false and no outputs_frontier/last_output_proof is given; flush_pending_outputs (3679-3697) asserts the host root equals the guest root (check_outputs_merkle_root defaults to true); run_advance_state_input (4718-4727) flushes before builder:end_input, where uarch_cycle_computation_hash_end_input (4458-4473) completes a period that lies after the input's stop. Manual doc/README.md ~2686-2715 ('The uarch cycle computation hash needs no epoch files ... Given a machine at the state that receives that input, begin_epoch:false with next_input_offset set to the input's zero-based offset in the epoch ... starts there').
candidates.description: The manual documents a shortcut for uarch computation hashes in a later input: load a machine at the state that receives input k, then pass begin_epoch:false,next_input_offset:k, without epoch files. In that mode the CLI's host-side outputs tree starts empty, but the guest's tx-buffer root commits to every output the application accepted before input k (template and earlier inputs). So at the target input's rx-accepted yield, flush_pending_outputs fails 'outputs Merkle root mismatch at input k' and the process exits 1. If the target period lies after the input's stop (the padded tail of the input, completed in end_input after the flush), the claim is never produced. If the period lies inside the input, the hash is printed but the run still exits with failure. The manual does not mention that outputs_frontier/last_output_proof or check_outputs_merkle_root:false are needed. The help for check_outputs_merkle_root says the host tree 'start[s] empty at genesis', which is the wrong state for a later input.
candidates.trigger: Any correctly designed application that accepted at least one output before the target input. An input sender only has to send inputs that cause outputs. The operator runs the documented shortcut command.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from a valid template: input 0 emits an output and is accepted, then the uarch hash of a period of input 1 is requested by the documented shortcut. Shown on the harness baremetal-template (emit-output guest).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion applies: the application is correctly designed, the command is the manual's, and no API misuse is involved. 2. Role: the CLI is Support. Section 3: Medium 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for ... a tool that computes claims'. 3. High/Medium cases: none matches directly. It is also a manual-versus-behavior contradiction on a claim-computation point: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' 4. In the honest-operator role this is an R4 violation ('From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim'; 'An application that breaks the rollup interface ... must never stop the honest operator from computing claims', and here the application does not even break it). That rating is Critical. Capped as Support: Medium. 5. Alternative: Low, if the shortcut is read as a development convenience and the user is expected to pass outputs_frontier. Same reading split as the confirmed R4-RGPLAYERGUEST-1, but here the guest is honest and the trigger is the documented procedure.
candidates.threat_to_goal: A tool that computes uarch-level claims for a period in a later input, the case the bottom-level dispute bisects to, cannot produce the claim by its documented procedure for any application with prior outputs. In the honest-operator role, the honest claim could not be posted in the inner tournament.
candidates.evidence: Scratch MANCLIROLL/u. input-0 'first-input-with-output' (accepted, 1 output) and input-1. Stored after0 = the machine after input 0 (--store). The reference run from the template, inputs 0..2, --uarch-cycle-computation-hash=log2_mcycle_period:10,mcycle_period_index:2^38+100000, prints 0xad98ec94.... The shortcut `--load=after0 --cmio-advance-state=input_file_index_begin:1,input_file_index_end:2,output_proof:,begin_epoch:false,next_input_offset:1` with the same uarch option prints no hash: it fails with 'cartesi-machine.lua:3692: outputs Merkle root mismatch at input 1' and exits 1. The same command with check_outputs_merkle_root:false prints 0xad98ec94... and exits 0. For period 2^38+2 (inside input 1), the shortcut prints the right hash 0xd65f291c... and then aborts with exit 1.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: from the baremetal-template, deliver one input that emits an output and store the machine. Then run the manual's shortcut for a period of input 1 after its stop. Assert exit status 0 and a hash equal to the from-template run of inputs 0..1 with begin_epoch:true. It fails today with exit 1 and no hash.

candidates.title: Stored revert mode, clean-exit site: a crash while the final remove of <dir>.revert is in progress leaves a half-removed .revert, and the documented recovery rule then discards the synced <dir>, the only intact copy (variant of R5-INVSTORE-2 at the exit path)
candidates.component: cartesi-machine CLI --revert-mode=stored exit path (src/cartesi-machine.lua 4924-4932, revert_stored.__index:remove_backup 3934-3939) and its recovery rule (help 172-175, doc/README.md ~2529-2537)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: the cartesi-machine CLI), standing in for an operator implementation that retains its machine.
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua 4924-4932 (destroy, sync_stored(<dir>), backup:remove_backup()); machine::remove_stored (src/machine.cpp 661-708) removes files one by one, config last; recovery text in the help (172-175) and doc/README.md ~2529-2537.
candidates.description: At a clean exit, the CLI destroys the machine, syncs <dir> (making it O2-guaranteed with the final accepted state) and then removes <dir>.revert file by file. A crash or kill during that removal leaves <dir> intact and synced, plus a <dir>.revert that still has its config.json but is missing data files. The documented rule ('If machine.revert exists, it holds that state, so discard machine and machine.revert.tmp and clone machine.revert back to machine'; help: 'resume from <directory>.revert if it exists') tells the operator to discard the good <dir> and clone the broken backup, which cannot be loaded. This is the mechanism of the confirmed R5-INVSTORE-2 (which concerns the commit site, where .tmp is discarded) at a second site. It is reported only so triage can confirm that the fix covers the exit path.
candidates.trigger: Process kill or crash (or power loss) during the final backup removal of a stored-mode run.
candidates.reachability: Every stored-mode run ends with this removal. The crash window is the removal of about 27 files.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? It needs a stop, but the directory the rule discards (<dir>) is O2-guaranteed: destroyed without a crash, then synced. The defect is the recovery rule, which reloads a directory that was being written (the half-removed .revert) and discards a guaranteed one. Possible reading: 'cleaning up after a stop' Medium case. 2. Role: Support. 3. Medium cases: 'A persistence operation that fails loudly ... while cleaning up after a stop' could cap it. 4. In the operator role: O2 ('resumes from a guaranteed one'), R4 restart. That rating is Critical. Capped as Support: Medium. 5. Same reading split as R5-INVSTORE-2 (Medium / Low / out of scope).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Following the manual's recovery procedure after a stop at the end of a run destroys the only durable copy of the epoch's final state.
candidates.evidence: killunlink.c, an LD_PRELOAD shim, SIGKILLs the process at the 86th unlink under *.revert/, i.e. the 5th file of the final remove_backup, during a 2-input stored-mode run on the baremetal-template. Afterwards: m loads (0xf973d2ab..., mcycle 13485809, equal to final.bin), m.revert exists but does not load ('unable to open backing file ... 0000000000000000-8000.bin'), and m.revert.tmp is absent. The documented rule selects m.revert.
candidates.test_idea: Same as the R5-INVSTORE-2 test, with the kill placed in the final removal: apply the manual's rule to the names left on disk and assert that the selected directory loads with the final hash.

not_covered: Fork revert mode with a live cartesi-jsonrpc-machine server: --remote-address=filename: address-file recording, rebinding after a rejected input, the 'fork keeps its own address and the client warns' path, --no-remote-create/--no-remote-destroy flows (read only, not run).

The Linux calculator example of the manual (rootfs-docs, calc.ext2): printed hashes, cycles and output files were not reproduced (long runs on a loaded 4-CPU host). All experiments used the harness baremetal-template (emit-output guest).

--print-mcycle-root-hashes example, --dump-memory-ranges file naming and content, --store-config/--load-config format inference, --append-bootargs/--no-bootargs, --log-step-uarch example output, --cmio-rx-buffer/--cmio-tx-buffer: read only (diagnostics).

Inspect-state queries in stored and fork modes (commit before the query, revert after) and the R4 rule that nothing from an inspect query reaches a state on the operator's path, beyond reading. In mode none an inspect query is not reverted and can reach --store and a sharing:all directory: documented ('DON'T USE ... IN PRODUCTION'), not reported.

Mode none: the manual says it 'never reverts rejected inputs', but the CLI aborts with the misleading 'rollback did not restore the input boundary' (the help says it aborts). Diagnostic only, not reported.

Resumable executions that change log2_mcycle_period and log2_bundle_mcycle_count while keeping their sum: the frontier file does not appear to record the leaf height, so the change may give a silently different hash. Documented as a 'must reuse' requirement (misuse), not tested.

The uarch shortcut with begin_epoch:false but next_input_offset omitted (defaults to 0, so the target period is counted from the wrong input, silently): misuse of a documented requirement, not tested.

Stored mode, first-commit window: <dir> is loaded with sharing:all, and get_root_hash runs, before any backup exists, so a crash there leaves no O2-guaranteed copy unless clone: was used. Formal O2 point, no demonstrable damage, not reported.

--final-hash combined with --max-mcycle in stored mode: the hash is printed for the interrupted machine before the exit-time revert to the committed state, so 'Loading machine after the command exits reproduces final-hash.bin' does not hold. Edge case, not reported.

--assert-rolling-template does not check reproducibility (iunrep) or the cmio HTIF configuration (yield automatic enabled, getchar disabled). Diagnostic gaps, not reported. Also not checked: the NOTE that the CLI 'prints' an initialization exception (only the yield banner is printed, and the exit status is non-zero only with --assert-rolling-template).

Checked and consistent: the CLI mcycle computation hash equals an independent naive reference (ref.lua: plain run plus get_root_hash at each 2^10-mcycle boundary, revert root hash after a rejection, run-length tree) on 4 inputs with a rejection (0xb990b9e7...); bundling (log2_bundle_mcycle_count 3) preserves it; a resumable split in stored mode with store/load across a rejected last input reproduces it; uarch period hashes from the template match the shortcut once outputs checking is disabled.

Crash-ordering between epoch files and stored-mode commits (output_hashes appended before the commit, other epoch files written after it): read; every inconsistency found is detected loudly on resume (state_hash or history-count checks), as documented ('may require manual repair').
